title: Alphabet stock sheds $700B as AI bills climb
excerpt: After leading the Magnificent 7 over much of the last 16 months, the tech giant is on shakier footing.
content_html:
Alphabet’s stock is down more than 15% from its May peak, wiping out roughly $700 billion in value, as concerns rise over its mounting AI bills and failure to produce a decisive technological breakthrough.

After leading the Magnificent 7 over much of the last 16 months, the tech giant is on shakier footing, having seen its top scientist depart, its brightest AI mind move to a different position, and delays to its newest Gemini model. But Google retains a superlative product suite, a “deep bench,” and a “long history of investing in AI,” a Wall Street Journal columnist argued, and a reshuffle — which has even seen Google co-founder Sergey Brin return to day-to-day operations — could be just what it needs.
